t:
(a) Fringe and Corridor Parking Facilities.—Section 137 of title 23, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in subsection (f)(1)—
            (A) by striking “104(b)(4)” and inserting “104(b)(1)”; and 
            (B) by inserting “including the addition of electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations,” after “new facilities,”; and  
        (2) by adding at the end the following:“(g) Funding.—The addition of electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations to new or previously funded parking facilities shall be eligible for funding under this section.”.  
    (b) Public Transportation.—Section 142(a)(1) of title 23, United States Code, is amended by inserting “, which may include electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations,” after “parking facilities”. 
    (c) Forest Development Roads and Trails.—Section 205(d) of title 23, United States Code, is amended by inserting “, which may include electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations,” after “parking areas”.

fable.w: The section only amends title 23 to make electric vehicle charging and natural gas refueling stations eligible for funding at parking facilities. The tempting reading is that the heading "Public Transportation" or the funding eligibility implies public involvement, but no outside party is consulted, heard, given a comment period, or granted a right to sue over a federal decision. Funding eligibility is not participation.
fable.s: The addition of electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations to new or previously funded parking facilities shall be eligible for funding under this section.

qwen_block.w: This section amends existing statutes to expand the types of infrastructure (specifically EV and natural gas charging stations) that are eligible for federal funding. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards involving non-federal parties. The text describes eligibility criteria for grants/funding, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The addition of electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations to new or previously funded parking facilities shall be eligible for funding under this section.

opus.w: This section only changes funding cross-references and makes electric vehicle charging stations and natural gas refueling stations eligible for funding at parking facilities, public transportation projects, and forest roads. One could argue that funding eligibility involves outside parties because states or others may apply for the money. But applying for funds does not count as participation, and nothing here requires consultation, public comment, rulemaking, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends existing statutes to make certain infrastructure improvements (EV charging stations) eligible for federal funding. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The definition of participation excludes applications for grants or funding eligibility determinations that do not involve a specific consultation or coordination requirement with non-federal parties prior to a decision.
qwen_chat.s: The addition of electric vehicle charging stations or natural gas vehicle refueling stations to new or previously funded parking facilities shall be eligible for funding under this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "public transportation" or "parking facilities," it implies public use or participation. However, the text only defines eligibility for federal funding for infrastructure improvements. It does not require any consultation, comment period, hearing, or advisory process involving non-federal parties before the decision to fund or build is made. The actors involved are federal agencies (implied by the statutory amendments to Title 23) and potentially state/local entities applying for funds, but the application process itself is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
